mainTopic: Measuring on יום טוב: the meaning of 'אבל לא במדה,' the honesty of אבא שאול בן בטנית, and when measuring is permitted.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous discussion of how people in different towns asked a butcher for meat on יום טוב without naming a price. A new משנה follows: you may ask a friend to fill a vessel on יום טוב, but not 'with a measure.' רבי יהודה is stricter about measuring vessels. The משנה also tells of אבא שאול בן בטנית, who filled his measures before יום טוב, and records two more views on why he did this. The גמרא gives two readings of 'not with a measure.' שמואל says it refers to a vessel set aside for measuring. רבא says it means only naming the measure out loud. Under each reading, the גמרא shows that רבי יהודה and the רבנן stay consistent with their views on weighing meat. A ברייתא tells how אבא שאול בן בטנית and his colleagues gave up wine and oil they might not have earned, and the גזברים sent it to צרכי רבים, such as public water pits. The amud ends with more rules about measuring on יום טוב and a dispute between רב and שמואל about measuring flour for חלה. אביי begins to respond to that dispute, and his response continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How different towns asked for portions without naming a price
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists the local phrases used in סורא, נרש, פומבדיתא, and נהר פקוד/מתא מחסיא to ask for a portion of meat on יום טוב without naming a price.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they would say: 'a תרטא or half a תרטא.' In נרש they would say: 'a part or half a part.' In פומבדיתא they would say: 'an אוזיא or half an אוזיא.' In נהר פקוד and מתא מחסיא they would say: 'a quarter or half a quarter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the topic on the previous amud. It lists the phrases each town used to ask a butcher for a portion of meat on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב you may not do business, so you cannot name a price or a weight. Each town had its own word for a familiar portion size. That let a person ask for meat without using the language of buying and selling.

keyTerms.meaning: a major Torah center in בבל
another major Torah center in בבל

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule against business-style language on יום טוב was followed in daily life, and that each place found its own permitted wording.

phrases.english: For in Sura they would say:
A tarta or half a tarta.
phrases.notes: A local name for a cut or portion of meat.

phrases.english: In Neresh they would say:
A part or half a part.
In Pumbedita they would say:
An uzya or half an uzya.
In Nehar Pekod and in Mata Meḥasya they would say:
A quarter or half a quarter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous amud's discussion of how to ask for meat on יום טוב without naming a price.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each town used a set portion name instead of a price or weight when buying meat on יום טוב.

steps.title: You may ask a friend to fill a vessel, but not with a measure
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא of the משנה rules that on יום טוב a person may ask a friend to fill a vessel for him, but not 'with a measure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may say to his friend on יום טוב, 'Fill this vessel for me,' but not with a measure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that you may borrow food on יום טוב by asking a friend to fill your vessel, but you may not do it by measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Filling a vessel is ordinary borrowing between neighbors and is allowed. Measuring makes it look like a weekday business transaction, so that is forbidden. The phrase 'אבל לא במדה' is unclear, and the גמרא will soon explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: a measure, or a measuring vessel

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person may say to his friend:
Fill this vessel for me,
but not with a measure.
phrases.notes: The גמרא will explain what this means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It continues the general theme of avoiding business-style dealings on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב you may ask someone to fill a vessel for you, but not with a measure.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids filling a measuring vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that if the vessel is a measuring vessel, you may not fill it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If the vessel was a measuring vessel, he may not fill it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a stricter opinion. If the container is a measuring vessel, it may not be filled on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allowed filling 'this vessel.' רבי יהודה adds a limit based on what kind of vessel it is. The גמרא gives two ways to define where he disagrees with the תנא קמא: שמואל's reading in steps 8–9, and רבא's reading in steps 13–14.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא; here he gives the stricter view

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If it was a measuring vessel,
he may not fill it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stricter opinion responding to the תנא קמא in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A measuring vessel may not be filled on יום טוב.

steps.title: The story of אבא שאול בן בטנית preparing measures before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells of אבא שאול בן בטנית, who filled his measures on ערב יום טוב and handed them to customers on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident with אבא שאול בן בטנית. He would fill his measures on ערב יום טוב and give them to his customers on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story about a shopkeeper who was also a חכם. He did all his measuring before יום טוב so he would not have to measure on יום טוב itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story supports the idea that measuring on יום טוב should be avoided. He handed out amounts already measured on ערב יום טוב, so customers got exact amounts without any measuring on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident; a story brought as an example
a תנא who was also a shopkeeper

steps.confusionAlert: אבא שאול בן בטנית in this story is a different person from אבא שאול, who speaks in the next step.

phrases.english: There was an incident with Abba Shaul ben Botnit,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִדּוֹתָיו מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: who would fill his measures on the eve of the Festival
and give them to the customers on the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing how to avoid measuring on יום טוב.
steps.raayaObject: That measuring on יום טוב itself should be avoided.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of אבא שאול בן בטנית, who measured everything on ערב יום טוב.

steps.title: אבא שאול: he did this even on חול המועד, so the measure would be clear
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול says the pre-filling was done even on חול המועד, so the measures would be accurate once the foam settled.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: He would do this even on חול המועד, because of making the measures clear.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול adds that the shopkeeper filled his measures ahead of time even on חול המועד. On those days measuring is allowed, so his reason must be something other than the laws of יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reason is accuracy. If a measure is filled early, the foam on the liquid settles. Then it is clear exactly how much is in it, and the customer is not cheated.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא, different from אבא שאול בן בטנית
חול המועד, the middle days of the festival
making the measures clear and accurate

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
Even on the intermediate Festival days he would do so,
because of the clarity of the measures.
phrases.notes: Letting the foam settle so the amount is exact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the story in step 4 and gives an honesty-based reason for the practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pre-filling measures was done even on חול המועד, to make the measures accurate.

steps.title: חכמים: he did this even on weekdays, so the measures would drain fully
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say he pre-filled measures even on ordinary weekdays, so the liquid would drain fully from the measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: He would do this even on a weekday, because of draining the measures.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים go further than אבא שאול. They say the shopkeeper did this even on regular weekdays, for an honesty reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a measure stands filled for a while, all the liquid drips out into the customer's vessel when it is poured. Then no liquid is left clinging inside, and the customer gets the full amount. This is a reason that applies every day, not just on festivals.

keyTerms.meaning: letting the measures drain out completely

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three views on the shopkeeper's practice. The story suggests he avoided measuring on יום טוב. אבא שאול says he did it on חול המועד for accuracy. The חכמים say he did it even on weekdays so the measures would drain fully.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Even on a weekday he would do so,
because of the draining of the measures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes beyond אבא שאול's view in step 5 and gives a different honesty reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pre-filling measures was done even on weekdays, so the liquid would drain out fully.

steps.title: What does 'but not with a measure' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'אבל לא במדה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'but not with a measure' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about unclear wording in the משנה. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not with a measure' could mean several things. It might mean not stating an amount, or not using a certain kind of vessel. The גמרא wants to pin down exactly what is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה (abbreviated גְּמָ׳)

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the meaning of: But not with a measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the תנא קמא's wording in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of the phrase 'אבל לא במדה' in the משנה.

steps.title: שמואל: only a vessel set aside for measuring is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, explains that only a vessel actually designated for measuring is forbidden. A vessel that is merely fit for measuring may be filled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: 'But not with a measure' means not with a vessel set aside for measuring. But a vessel that is merely fit for measuring may be filled.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. The תנא קמא forbids only a vessel that is actually used as a measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל separates two kinds of vessels. A 'מיוחד למדה' is actually set aside as a measure, and it is forbidden. A 'עומד למדה' could be used as a measure but is not yet used that way, and the תנא קמא permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא and student of שמואל
fit for measuring but not yet used for it

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה (the אמורא quoting שמואל) is not the same person as רבי יהודה (the תנא in the משנה).

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
But not with a vessel designated for measuring.
But a vessel that stands to be used for measuring, he may fill it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Not with a measure' means not with a vessel designated for measuring. A vessel merely fit for measuring is permitted.

steps.title: So רבי יהודה forbids even a vessel that is only fit for measuring
steps.stepSummary: Following שמואל's explanation, רבי יהודה is understood as forbidding even a vessel that is only fit for measuring.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה comes to say that even a vessel that is fit for measuring may not be filled.
steps.whatsHappening: Using שמואל's explanation, the גמרא now defines the disagreement in the משנה. רבי יהודה is stricter and also forbids the vessel that the תנא קמא allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא already forbids a vessel set aside for measuring, רבי יהודה must be adding something new. His addition is the 'עומד למדה' vessel. So the dispute is only about a vessel that could be used for measuring but has not been used that way yet.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, all agree that a vessel set aside for measuring is forbidden on יום טוב. They disagree about a vessel that is only fit for measuring. The תנא קמא permits it, and רבי יהודה forbids it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda comes to say
that even a vessel that stands to be used for measuring
he may not fill it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies שמואל's explanation from step 8 to define רבי יהודה's view from step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא קמא forbids only a vessel set aside for measuring. רבי יהודה forbids even a vessel that is only fit for measuring.

steps.title: Both opinions seem to flip compared to the meat-weighing משנה
steps.stepSummary: Based on שמואל's reading, רבי יהודה is strict and the רבנן are lenient. In the meat-weighing משנה, רבי יהודה is lenient and the רבנן are strict. So each opinion seems to contradict itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that about the joy of יום טוב, רבי יהודה is strict and the רבנן are lenient? But we heard them say the opposite! As we learned: רבי יהודה says a person may weigh meat against a vessel or against a cleaver. The חכמים say we do not look at the pan of a scale at all. So there רבי יהודה is lenient and the רבנן are strict. רבי יהודה contradicts רבי יהודה, and the רבנן contradict the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the opinions in our משנה side by side with an earlier משנה about weighing meat. It shows that each side seems to switch positions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל, רבי יהודה forbids even a vessel that is only fit for measuring, and the רבנן allow it. In the meat case, רבי יהודה lets you weigh against a pot or cleaver, while the חכמים forbid using a scale at all. So the strict side and the lenient side seem to trade places.

keyTerms.meaning: So it seems / evidently (draws a conclusion)
The joy of the festival (the reason we allow food preparation)
The pan of a balance scale

steps.confusionAlert: This is not one contradiction. It is two separate ones: רבי יהודה against himself, and the רבנן against themselves. The next two steps answer each one separately.

phrases.english: So it seems that regarding the joy of the festival
Rabbi Yehuda is strict
and the Rabbis are lenient?
But we heard them say the opposite!
As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
a person may weigh meat
against a vessel or against a cleaver,
and the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: one may not look at the pan of a scale at all.
So Rabbi Yehuda is lenient
and the Rabbis are strict.
Rabbi Yehuda contradicts Rabbi Yehuda,
and the Rabbis contradict the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the positions that came out of שמואל's reading in steps 8-9
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יהודה and the רבנן under שמואל's reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In our משנה, רבי יהודה is strict and the רבנן are lenient. In the meat-weighing משנה, רבי יהודה is lenient and the רבנן are strict. So each side contradicts itself.

steps.title: Answering רבי יהודה: a pot or cleaver is not fit for measuring
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction for רבי יהודה. A pot or cleaver is not fit for measuring, so he allows it. A vessel here that is fit for measuring is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between רבי יהודה and רבי יהודה there is no difficulty: there it is a thing that is not fit for measuring; here it is a thing that is fit for measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first contradiction by showing that רבי יהודה is talking about two different kinds of objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pot or cleaver is not a measuring tool at all, so weighing against it does not look like real measuring. A vessel that could serve as a measure looks too much like weekday measuring, so רבי יהודה forbids it. His standard stays the same in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit or ready to be used as a measure

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yehuda there is no difficulty:
there, it is with something not fit for measuring,
here, it is with something fit for measuring.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction in step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to change his strictness from case to case
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה forbids anything fit for measuring and allows things that are not fit for measuring, like a pot or cleaver

steps.title: Answering the רבנן: a scale is weekday behavior, a plain vessel is not
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction for the רבנן. Using a scale is acting like a weekday, so they forbid it. Filling a vessel that is not a real measure is not weekday behavior, so they allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between the רבנן and the רבנן there is also no difficulty: there he is acting the way people act on a weekday; here he is not acting the way people act on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second contradiction by showing that the רבנן care about whether the act looks like weekday business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weighing meat on a scale is exactly what a butcher does on an ordinary day, so the רבנן forbid even looking at the scale. Filling a vessel that is not set aside for measuring does not look like weekday measuring, so they allow it. Their test is the same in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The way people do it on a weekday

steps.whatToRemember: Under שמואל: רבי יהודה's test is whether the object is fit for measuring. The רבנן's test is whether the act looks like weekday behavior. Both sides stay consistent.

phrases.english: Between the Rabbis and the Rabbis there is also no difficulty:
there, he is acting the way people act on a weekday,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא לָא קָא עָבֵיד כִּדְעָבְדִין בְּחוֹל.
phrases.english: here, he is not acting the way people act on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction in step 10 and closes the discussion of שמואל's reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (weekday-like act vs. not)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seemed lenient here but strict about the scale
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן forbid only acts that look like weekday business

steps.title: רבא's different reading: just do not say the name of a measure
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'אבל לא במדה' only means you may not say a measure's name out loud. You may even fill a vessel that is set aside for measuring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What does 'but not by measure' mean? That he should not mention the name of a measure to him. But a vessel set aside for measuring, he may fill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a second, different answer to the question from step 7 about what 'אבל לא במדה' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the problem was the vessel itself. For רבא, the problem is only the words: saying 'fill me a קב' sounds like weekday business. Under רבא, even a real measuring vessel may be filled, as long as no amount is named.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of a measure (e.g., 'a קַב')
A vessel set aside for measuring

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not adding to שמואל. He is giving a whole new reading. Under רבא, the תנא קמא allows even a real measuring vessel, which is more lenient than שמואל's reading.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the meaning of 'but not by measure'?
That he should not mention to him the name of a measure,
but a vessel set aside for measuring, he may fill.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מַאי אֲבָל לֹא בְּמִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question in step 7 and offers another answer instead of שמואל's
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'אבל לא במדה' in the משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It forbids only saying the name of a measure. Filling even a dedicated measuring vessel is allowed.

steps.title: Under רבא, רבי יהודה forbids filling a real measuring vessel
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, רבי יהודה comes to add that a vessel set aside for measuring may not be filled, even without naming a measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה comes to say: a vessel set aside for measuring, he may not fill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יהודה's opinion means according to רבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids only naming the measure. רבי יהודה goes further and forbids using a real measuring vessel at all. A vessel that is merely fit for measuring is still allowed even according to רבי יהודה here.

keyTerms.meaning: And he comes to say (introduces what a view adds)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of the משנה. שמואל: the תנא קמא forbids a dedicated measuring vessel, and רבי יהודה also forbids a vessel fit for measuring. רבא: the תנא קמא forbids only naming the measure, and רבי יהודה also forbids a dedicated measuring vessel.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda comes to say:
a vessel set aside for measuring, he may not fill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's reading by placing רבי יהודה's opinion within it, parallel to step 9 for שמואל
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under רבא, the תנא קמא forbids only naming a measure, while רבי יהודה also forbids filling a vessel set aside for measuring.

steps.title: Each opinion seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: Here רבי יהודה is strict and the רבנן are lenient about measuring for שמחת יום טוב. In the meat-weighing משנה, רבי יהודה is lenient and the רבנן are strict. So each side seems to contradict itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems that for festival joy, רבי יהודה is strict and the רבנן are lenient. But we heard them say the opposite! In the משנה, רבי יהודה says a person may weigh meat against a vessel or a cleaver. The חכמים say you may not even look at a scale's pans. So there, רבי יהודה is lenient and the רבנן are strict. That is a contradiction for each of them.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on רבא's reading that רבי יהודה forbids filling a vessel set aside for measuring, the גמרא points out that both sides now seem to flip their positions compared to the meat-weighing משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our case רבי יהודה adds a restriction and the רבנן permit. In the earlier משנה (28a), רבי יהודה permits weighing meat against a pot or cleaver, while the חכמים ban any use of a scale. Neither side seems consistent, so the גמרא states the contradiction twice: once for רבי יהודה and once for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It seems / apparently (introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said)
We heard them say the opposite
The pan of a balance scale
A contradiction between one statement of a person and another statement of the same person

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a fight between רבי יהודה and the רבנן. Each side is being checked against its own words in another משנה.

phrases.english: Apparently, regarding the joy of the festival,
Rabbi Yehuda is strict and the Rabbis are lenient?
But we heard them say the opposite!
As we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A person may weigh meat
against a vessel or against a cleaver,
and the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: One may not look at the pans of a scale at all.
phrases.notes: Even using a scale with a pot or cleaver as the counterweight is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְקוּלָּא וְרַבָּנַן לְחוּמְרָא.
phrases.english: So apparently Rabbi Yehuda is lenient and the Rabbis are strict.
Rabbi Yehuda contradicts Rabbi Yehuda,
and the Rabbis contradict the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבא's conclusion (רבי יהודה adds a restriction) and checks it against the meat-weighing משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of both רבי יהודה and the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their strict and lenient positions flip between two משניות about measuring on יום טוב.

steps.title: Resolving רבי יהודה: is the vessel set aside for measuring?
steps.stepSummary: Weighing against a pot or cleaver is allowed because they are not measuring tools. Here the vessel is set aside for measuring, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no contradiction for רבי יהודה. There, the item is not set aside for measuring. Here, the vessel is set aside for measuring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first half of the contradiction: it shows that רבי יהודה is consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pot or cleaver is an everyday kitchen tool, not a real measure, so weighing against it is permitted. A vessel that is set aside for measuring is a real measuring tool, so filling it is forbidden. רבי יהודה follows one rule in both places: what matters is the item's status as a measure.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult:
there, it is something not set aside for measuring,
here, it is set aside for measuring.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבי יהודה half of the contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (the type of vessel)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה is lenient about measuring in one place and strict in another.
steps.terutzMaskana: He forbids only items set aside for measuring. A pot or cleaver is not one of them.

steps.title: Resolving the רבנן: does it look like weekday business?
steps.stepSummary: Using a scale looks like weekday business, so it is forbidden. Serving wine in a measuring cup is something people normally do, so it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is also no contradiction for the רבנן. There, he acts the way people act on a weekday. Here, he does not, because people normally serve wine in a measuring cup and drink from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second half of the contradiction: it shows that the רבנן are consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the test is whether the action looks like commerce (עובדין דחול). Putting meat on a scale is a typical shop activity. Measuring cups are commonly used just to serve wine to guests, so filling one does not look like business.

keyTerms.meaning: As people do on a weekday (weekday-style activity)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה asks, 'Is this a real measuring tool?' The רבנן ask, 'Does this look like weekday business?' With those two questions, both sides are consistent.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult:
there, he acts as people do on a weekday,
here, he does not act as people do on a weekday,
for people commonly
serve wine in a measuring vessel and drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן half of the contradiction, finishing the answer begun in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (weekday-like action or not)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן are strict about scales but lenient about measures, which looks inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: They forbid only actions that look like commerce. Serving wine in a measuring cup does not.

steps.title: אבא שאול בן בטנית also did this on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's story of אבא שאול בן בטנית. A ברייתא adds that he prepared measures ahead of time even on חול המועד, so he would not lose time from the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה tells a story about אבא שאול בן בטנית. A ברייתא taught: he did this even on חול המועד, to avoid wasting time from the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה: the story of אבא שאול בן בטנית, who filled his measures before יום טוב. A ברייתא adds a detail to that story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Measuring is allowed on חול המועד, so he did not need to prepare in advance. He still filled the measures at night, ahead of time, so he could spend his day learning without stopping to serve customers.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the intermediate days of the festival
Losing time from learning in the study hall

steps.confusionAlert: On חול המועד he prepared early to protect his learning time, not because measuring was forbidden.

phrases.english: There was an incident with Abba Shaul ben Botnit.
phrases.notes: This quotes the line from the משנה being explained.

phrases.english: A Tanna taught: even on the intermediate festival days he would do so,
because of losing time from the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of measuring and begins explaining the משנה's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול בן בטנית prepared measures in advance even on חול המועד, to protect his learning time.

steps.title: אבא שאול בן בטנית and his friends give away profit they may not have earned
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that אבא שאול בן בטנית gathered 300 jugs of wine from foam in his measures. His friends gathered 300 jugs of oil from drips left in theirs. They brought everything to the גזברים in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: he gathered 300 jugs of wine from the 'clearing' of his measures. His friends gathered 300 jugs of oil from the 'draining' of theirs. They brought them to the Temple treasurers in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about אבא שאול בן בטנית that shows how careful he was about honesty in measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול בן בטנית worried that foam on top of the wine meant customers got a little less than they paid for. He set aside the wine that he thought might not be his. His friends worried that oil left clinging to their measures was not fully given over to the buyer. Since they could not return it to the right owners, they brought it to the גזברים in ירושלים. The next steps show that the גזברים told them they did not need to do this, and then told them to use it for צרכי רבים.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'clearing' of measures: wine that may have been shorted because of foam
The 'draining' of measures: oil left clinging inside the vessel

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how strict great people were about honesty in business. Even tiny amounts that might belong to someone else were set aside.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא כָּנַס שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי יַיִן
phrases.english: He gathered three hundred jugs of wine
from the clearing of the measures (the foam),

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲבֵרָיו כָּנְסוּ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי שֶׁמֶן
phrases.english: and his colleagues gathered three hundred jugs of oil
from the draining of the measures,
and they brought them before the treasurers in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּא כָּנַס שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא about the same person from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול בן בטנית and his friends set aside any wine and oil that might not have been rightfully theirs and brought it to the Temple treasurers.

steps.title: The treasurers say there is no need, and the merchants refuse to keep it
steps.stepSummary: The גזברים tell אבא שאול and his friends they do not need to return the wine and oil. The merchants answer that they still do not want to keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The treasurers said to them: You do not need to do this. They answered: We also do not want to keep it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא story continues. The גזברים and the merchants have a short back-and-forth about the leftover wine and oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזברים mean that buyers already know about the foam and the drips and give them up, so this is not stolen property. The merchants answer that, just as the buyers do not want it, they themselves also do not want to benefit from it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: אִי אַתֶּם זְקוּקִים לְכָךְ.
phrases.english: They (the treasurers) said to them: You are not required to do this.
phrases.notes: The buyers already gave up their claim to the foam and drips.

phrases.english: They (the merchants) said to them: We too
do not wish to benefit from this.
phrases.notes: An act of extra carefulness, beyond the strict law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: אִי אַתֶּם זְקוּקִים לְכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 19 about the 300 jugs brought to the גזברים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Strictly, the leftovers are not stolen, but the merchants chose not to keep them anyway.

steps.title: The treasurers tell them to use it for public needs
steps.stepSummary: Since the merchants were strict with themselves, the גזברים tell them to use the wine and oil for צרכי רבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to them: Since you are strict with yourselves, use them for public needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a solution. The wine and oil go to projects that help the whole public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The merchants could not return the leftovers to the many separate buyers. Using it for the public is a way to give it back to everyone together, which would include those buyers.

keyTerms.meaning: Public needs, projects that help the whole community

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: הוֹאִיל וְהֶחְמַרְתֶּם עַל עַצְמְכֶם —
phrases.english: They said to them: Since you were strict with yourselves —
use them for public needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ending of the exchange in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property you cannot return to its owners should go to צרכי רבים.

steps.title: Source: a thief who doesn't know whom he robbed uses it for public needs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who stole and does not know from whom should use it for צרכי רבים, and this supports the advice of the גזברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If someone stole and does not know from whom he stole, he should use it for public needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the advice of the גזברים has a legal source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you cannot find the owner, giving to the public helps everyone, and the owner is part of that public. The merchants' case is similar: many unknown buyers, so the public is the right place for it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
If one stole and does not know from whom he stole —
he should use them for public needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: גָּזַל וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מִמִּי גָּזַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the advice in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: Using the leftover wine and oil for צרכי רבים
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: one who stole from an unknown person uses it for צרכי רבים

steps.title: What counts as public needs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly צרכי רבים are.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to define the term. This sets up רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The term צרכי רבים is general. The גמרא wants to know exactly what kind of public project is meant.

phrases.english: What are they (public needs)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term from Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What projects count as צרכי רבים

steps.title: רב חסדא: cisterns, ditches, and caves
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that צרכי רבים means digging water pits that everyone can use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Cisterns, ditches, and caves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question with clear examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These water holes are used by all travelers. So the owner of the stolen item will probably benefit from them too.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Cisterns, ditches, and caves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בּוֹרוֹת, שִׁיחִין וּמְעָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צרכי רבים are public water pits: בורות, שיחין, ומערות.
steps.whatToRemember: If you cannot return property to its owner, use it for צרכי רבים, like public water pits, so that everyone, including the owner, benefits.

steps.title: רבנא עוקבא's lecture: when measuring is allowed on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבנא עוקבא teaches: you may not measure barley for an animal on יום טוב, but you may scoop it out with a vessel without being exact. A baker may measure spices so that the food is not ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא authorized רבנא עוקבא to lecture, and he taught: A person may not measure barley and put it before his animal on יום טוב. But he may scoop out a קב or two and put it before his animal without worry. And a baker may measure spices and put them in his pot, so that he does not ruin his dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about measuring on יום טוב. רבנא עוקבא gives three rules in one lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exact measuring looks like weekday business, so it is forbidden. Scooping a rough amount is not real measuring, so it is fine. Spices are allowed because the measuring is needed for the food itself, since too much would ruin it.

keyTerms.meaning: He appointed him, authorized him to lecture
Scoops out (digs a hole in the pile) with a vessel

steps.confusionAlert: Using a vessel that holds a קב is not counted as measuring here, because he scoops without caring about the exact amount.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַבָּנָא עוּקְבָא, וּדְרַשׁ:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda authorized Rabbana Ukva, and he taught:
A person may not measure barley
and put it before his animal on Yom Tov,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קוֹדֵר הוּא קַב אוֹ קַבִּים
phrases.english: but he may scoop out a kav or two kav
and put it before his animal, and he need not worry.
And a baker may measure spices
and put them into his pot,
so that he does not spoil his dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַבָּנָא עוּקְבָא, וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of אבא שאול בן בטנית ends, the גמרא opens a new section of teachings about when measuring is allowed on יום טוב. It shares the general theme of the משנה but does not build on the earlier contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exact measuring of animal feed is forbidden. Rough scooping is allowed. Measuring spices is allowed so the food is not spoiled.

steps.title: רב: a woman may measure flour for חלה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a woman may measure flour on יום טוב so that she knows how much חלה to separate and can give it generously.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: A woman may measure flour on יום טוב and put it into her dough, so that she can separate חלה generously.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another measuring case, this time from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she knows the exact amount of dough, she can separate the right amount of חלה. Since measuring helps with a מצוה, רב allows it, like the spices.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
A woman may measure flour on Yom Tov
and put it into her dough
so that she separates challah generously.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case of allowed measuring to the list in Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measuring flour for proper separation of חלה is allowed on יום טוב.

steps.title: שמואל: measuring flour is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and forbids measuring the flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposite ruling, so now there is a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that she can just estimate the amount of חלה, so measuring is not needed. Without a real need, measuring stays forbidden, like with the barley.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measuring flour for חלה on יום טוב is forbidden.

steps.title: But שמואל's own school taught that it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: a ברייתא from שמואל's own school says measuring flour is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in the school of שמואל that it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling with a source from his own school. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is strange for שמואל to forbid something that his own school's ברייתא allows. The גמרא will need to explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so? (opens a challenge)
A ברייתא taught in the school of שמואל

phrases.english: But didn't the school of Shmuel teach,
that it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in Step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that measuring flour is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא from שמואל's own school says it is permitted, which contradicts his ruling.

steps.title: אביי restates the clash between שמואל and his own school
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens his response by laying out the two conflicting positions: שמואל himself said measuring flour is forbidden, but the ברייתא of דבי שמואל says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Now that שמואל said it is forbidden, and the school of שמואל taught that it is permitted,
steps.whatsHappening: אביי restates the contradiction from the last step: שמואל forbids measuring, but his own school's ברייתא allows it. This is a setup line. אביי is preparing to say what we should do in light of both opinions, and that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled yet. אביי accepts both facts as true and does not try to explain the contradiction away. The word הַשְׁתָּא ("now that") signals that a practical conclusion is about to follow from these two facts.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from בבל who here responds to the contradiction
"Now that...": opens a conclusion based on facts already established
"It was taught in the school of שמואל": a ברייתא from שמואל's study house

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי is saying שמואל was refuted. He treats both the ruling and the ברייתא as valid, and he is building toward a practical way to handle both.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line, merged into the statement it introduces.

phrases.english: Now that Shmuel said it is forbidden,
and the school of Shmuel taught that it is permitted,
phrases.notes: Refers back to the ברייתא cited in Step 28. The sentence continues into אביי's conclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the קשיא in Step 28 by restating both sides of the contradiction as the basis for a practical conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: אביי takes as given that שמואל forbids measuring and that דבי שמואל permits it. His practical guidance follows in the next line.
